title: Pajeori Korean Scallion Salad
shortDescription: Fine scallion threads are soaked until crisp, dried, and tossed at the last minute with gochugaru, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
culturalContext: Pajeori is a sharp, fresh scallion accompaniment commonly served with Korean grilled meat. It is also called pa muchim in many contexts; cut, dressing, sweetness, and chile intensity vary, so naming and framing remain queued for Korean review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Chef’s knife and cutting board or scallion slicer with guard

ingredients.preparation: cut into 10 cm / 4-inch fine lengthwise threads

instructions.heading: Wash and trim
instructions.action: Wash scallions thoroughly under cool running water, removing grit between outer layers, then trim roots and damaged tips.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Scallions are crisp, clean, and free of slime or grit.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean sink and produce-only board and discard slimy scallions.

instructions.heading: Cut fine threads
instructions.action: Cut scallions into 10 cm / 4-inch sections, then slice lengthwise into fine threads, or use a guarded scallion slicer on a stable board.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Threads are long, thin, and similar in width.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep fingertips behind the blade and use the slicer guard; stop before pieces become too short to control.

instructions.heading: Crisp
instructions.action: Soak scallion threads in ice water for 10 minutes, separating them gently by hand.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Threads curl slightly and feel crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Use potable water and a clean bowl.

instructions.heading: Dry
instructions.action: Drain thoroughly and spin dry or blot with clean towels.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No free water remains to dilute the dressing.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a cleaned spinner and fresh towel to avoid recontamination.

instructions.heading: Mix and toss
instructions.action: Whisk gochugaru, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds until the sugar begins to dissolve. Add scallions and toss gently just before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Threads are lightly coated and remain springy, with little liquid pooling.
instructions.safetyNote: Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens and use clean utensils.

instructions.heading: Serve immediately
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean bowl and serve at once alongside cooked grilled food.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Scallions remain crisp and curled rather than limp.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the salad and its utensils separate from raw meat at a tabletop grill.

grillSetup: No grill is used for the salad; serve it on the cooked-food side of the table and keep it away from raw-meat tongs and splatter.
visualDonenessCues: Scallion threads are clean, fine, curled, and crisp
Salad is lightly coated without pooled water
foodSafetyNotes: Wash scallions thoroughly under cool potable running water.
Use guarded cutting technique and a stable board.
Dry scallions with clean equipment before dressing.
Keep ready-to-eat salad separate from raw meat and raw-food utensils.
Refrigerate undressed scallions at or below 40°F / 4°C and discard dressed salad after extended service.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify packaged ingredients and prevent raw-meat or shared-utensil cross-contact.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after checking the full label.
Thinly sliced spring onion greens may work, but the texture and bite require testing.
ingredientSourcing: Choose large, crisp scallions with dry white bases and vivid green tops.
A guarded Korean scallion slicer can make uniform threads but is optional.
makeAhead: Cut, crisp, and dry scallions up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate covered; mix dressing separately and toss at serving.
storage: Store undressed scallion threads and dressing separately under refrigeration for up to 1 day. Dressed salad is best immediately and should be discarded after 2 hours at room temperature.
leftovers: Dressed leftovers wilt quickly; use only continuously refrigerated salad within 1 day and discard any table-exposed portion with uncertain handling.
servingSuggestions: Pile beside grilled beef or pork
Use a small bundle inside a lettuce wrap

faq.question: Why soak the scallion threads?
faq.answer: A short ice-water soak firms the cut edges, encourages curling, and moderates some of the sharp raw bite.

faq.question: Can I dress pajeori ahead?
faq.answer: Keep the components separate and toss immediately before serving because salt and vinegar quickly soften the scallions.
